What the lab recommends

Nothing changes in the live paper bots until Ben says yes. These are proposals, ranked strongest first.

Exhibit A · overfitting test

Did the backtest predict the future?

Each dot is one strategy. Across: Sharpe ratio in the design period. Up: Sharpe in the held-out years nobody tuned on. If backtests predicted the future, the dots would climb to the right. The dashed lines mark the benchmark.

Exhibit B · selection test

Picking last year's winners

Every January, buy the strategies with the best Sharpe over the previous few years, from the whole pool, and hold them for 12 months. This is what chasing backtests does in practice.

Exhibit C · finalists

Growth of $1, design years and held-out years

Pick any finalist to overlay it on the benchmark. Log scale, so equal slopes mean equal percentage growth. The shaded part is the held-out test.

Exhibit D · the gates

Finalists against the seven gates

G1 design-period merit (top quarter and deflated Sharpe ≥ 0.8) · G2 beats the benchmark's held-out Sharpe with a shallower drawdown · G3 bootstrap says the win is probably real (≥ 80%) · G4 beats 95% of random monkeys trading the same way · G5 still wins at 2.5× costs · G6 its parameter neighbours also work · G7 makes at least as much as a 60/40 portfolio (crypto: half of BTC).

Method

How the lab keeps itself honest

  1. Data: daily adjusted closes from Yahoo for 50 ETFs back to 1993 (bonds, gold, sectors, countries) and 4 coins back to 2014, in US dollars. Cash earns the 13-week T-bill rate.
  2. Split: ETFs are designed on 2005–2016 and judged on 2017–now. Crypto is designed on 2016–2020 and judged on 2021–now. Seven research agents built their grids without seeing the held-out years.
  3. Costs: 0.10% per trade for ETFs and 0.30% for crypto, re-tested at 0.25% / 0.60% and on a 0–0.50% ladder.
  4. Look-ahead audit: every strategy was re-run on data cut at 38 dates; any weight that changed would reveal a peek at the future. Leaks found: .
  5. Luck controls: deflated Sharpe ratio using the number of independent strategy clusters, a block bootstrap against the benchmark, 200 random "monkey" portfolios per trading style, the probability of backtest overfitting (CSCV), and a rebalance-day shift test.
  6. Known limits: ETF universes are survivorship-safe, but the ETFs and some rules were chosen by people who know recent history. Results are in dollars; the GBP view in Exhibit C converts at the daily exchange rate. Taxes are ignored.

Built by Claude for Ben's Stocks project. Simulated paper research; past performance does not predict future results. Code: /mnt/project-files/strategy-lab.
